Same thing. A replacement set may be substituted; DCS-Bridge carries records with the set gone.
The component the built-ins run in: DCS-Bridge's Lua half in the mission-scripting state. Specified in SPEC 6, not here.

The other DCS-side component, in the GameGUI hook state. Its own built-ins are HOOK. Owns player identity and lifecycle, chat, roster, kick, slot, bans, server control, the projection derivation and magnetic declination.
The single DCS-Bridge-owned file holding every built-in handler. A release overwrites it.
SPEC 13.1 key that skips a shipped file at a mission reload. The durable way to disable a built-in.
Tier 1 is sized on demand shown by existing tooling, Tier 2 on need it does not cover, Tier 3 on stated refusals. A gap is weaker evidence than a covered case.
The first-release record and command set: proven demand, low cost, nothing that is a research problem.

column3: 3. Tier 2 — what the catalogue's gaps ask for
column4: What existing tooling has left unbuilt after five years, led by complete coalition.addGroup.
Deliberate exclusions with a stated reason each: text-to-speech and SRS, env logging, dostring_in exposure, weapon static descriptors.
Every built-in runs in the mission-scripting state and declares no target option. The division from the hook driver is by Lua state, not by taste.
SPEC 5.2 inbound ring for mission-scripting-targeted topics. Every built-in topic routes here.
Every position a built-in emits is DCS-local: +x north, +z east, +y up. SPEC 8.2 pins it.

Transverse Mercator on WGS84, k_0 = 0.9996, a central meridian at one of sixty UTM zone values, and a per-terrain false easting and northing. DCS-Bridge derives and publishes it; the built-ins only obey the convention it reads.
The hook driver identifying the projection each epoch: one converted point, a sixty-way meridian search, one checked point. Not a least-squares fit.
The textual encoding CoordinateCalibration carries, +proj=tmerc with the derived meridian and origin. Never an EPSG code: a re-origined UTM zone cannot have one.
Three or four point-pairs a consumer checks the published parameters against, rather than fits them from. They also carry the declination.
DCS-Bridge's own LIFECYCLE record, emitted by the hook driver. Carries the projection parameters, the PROJ string, the verification points and their declination. No built-in contributes to it.
DCS +x. The reference for any heading derived from carried data.
Differs from grid north by the projection's convergence angle, which the published parameters give a consumer at no cost.
The grid-to-true difference, recoverable from the published projection.
Magnetic declination, optional per verification point on CoordinateCalibration. The hook driver's from end to end: magvar lives in the gui state, which no built-in can reach.
The built-in batch conversion command. Wraps LLtoMGRS and MGRStoLL only; LOtoLL and LLtoLO are redundant once the projection is published.
SPEC 13.1 cap on one ConvertCoords request. Above it, a CommandAck with outcome REFUSED.
Measured approximate, not exact: coord.LLtoMGRS and the map's own routine agree on zone, band, digraph and easting and differ by a metre in the northing at four of six sampled points.
DCS carries positions as single-precision floats, so a coordinate round-tripped through coord.* comes back quantised. The precision floor under every derived parameter.
The per-weapon data that exists only while the weapon flies: launcher, target, position, velocity, type name. Carried.
Weapon type constants — warhead, calibre, guidance, envelopes. Not carried per weapon, and no bulk export replaces them.
An opt-in subscription with a three-term filter, sampling weapons in flight under max_tracked_weapons.
SPEC 13.1 resource cap on weapons held. weapon_max_samples throttles at half its depth.
SPEC 6.7 cap. A weapon-tracking subscription counts against it; the weapons it holds do not.
The only binding reaching weapon descriptor data without a live weapon object. Returns nil, not an empty table, on a unit carrying nothing.
A managed laser or infrared designation resource with a driver-side tracking loop, rather than a create/update/destroy primitive triple.
Creates a laser spot and returns its handle in a typed reply. Declares reply_to and carries both request_id and idempotency_key.
Destroys a laser spot by handle.
The infrared twin of LaserOn, identical in shape minus the code.
The infrared twin of LaserOff.
SPEC 13.1 resource cap. Above it, a CommandAck with outcome REFUSED.
Validated as an integer in 0 to 9999, with no band enforced. Nothing on the scripted path validates it: the engine accepted 10000, wrapped -1 to 4294967295 and truncated 1.5 to 1.
The AH-64D cockpit's code-range list. A display table, not a validator.
A spot outlives the destruction of its source unit — code, point and category all still answer, and setPoint still moves the beam. The driver must detect that itself.

column4: Four static members on SceneryObject, Unit, StaticObject and Airbase. The three usable ones are one lookup under three names and ignore the class called on; only the SceneryObject member crashes.
SPEC 13.1 key, default false, gating a handler that reaches a crasher-register binding.
A defensive check against a binding that answers with something unexpected rather than raising, which no blacklist probe finds. Binds any handler in this state, not only the built-ins.
SPEC 8.1 transport drop policy. Built-in records are DURABLE or COMMAND; none is LIFECYCLE.
SPEC 14.4 per-topic gate. The built-ins use read and command, and define none of their own.
Built-in records forward S_EVENT_* payloads as DCS defines them, with no smoothed abstractions.
